Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage across major business and general-news outlets is dominated by the fallout from Tuesday's US midterm elections, in which Democrats swept both chambers of Congress, triggering a historic rally in stocks and bonds, a plunge in oil prices, and a scramble to identify corporate winners and losers. A secondary cluster of stories covers CVS Health's major corporate breakup, announced the same day, and the political and market fallout for Elon Musk's companies after Democratic wins in Texas.

stories.headline: Democratic sweep of Congress sparks historic market rally as oil plunges
stories.summary: The Dow jumped roughly 1,500 points and oil prices slid as Democrats swept Congress, with crude dropping on hopes the Iran war could wind down; CNBC reported the rally as the Dow's best day in 18 months after Trump's acceptance of the results removed political uncertainty.

stories.headline: CVS Health to split into two public companies in major healthcare breakup
stories.summary: CVS Health announced plans to separate its retail pharmacy business from its insurance and pharmacy-benefits divisions by 2028, reversing the vertically integrated model it built through its $78 billion Aetna acquisition; CNBC noted shares fell about 10% on the news even as some analysts said the move could ease regulatory pressure.

stories.headline: Musk's Tesla and SpaceX shares tumble after Texas Democratic wins
stories.summary: Elon Musk's companies came under investor scrutiny after Democrats won unexpected victories in his adopted home state of Texas, part of a broader Democratic sweep of Congress; NYT reported Musk-backed candidates lost in Texas as Democrats signaled intent to investigate him.

stories.headline: Wall Street braces for 2027 debt-ceiling showdown under divided government
stories.summary: Wall Street strategists warned that the return of divided government after Democrats took Congress could unsettle bond markets next year by setting up a bruising fight over the debt ceiling.

stories.headline: Trump Media stock sinks to all-time low after midterm rebuke
stories.summary: Shares in Trump Media & Technology Group fell more than 13% in early trading to about $5.10, extending a slide that has cut the stock more than 60% this year, after Democrats swept Congress.

stories.headline: US trade deficit stays elevated despite Trump tariffs
stories.summary: The gap between US exports and imports remained relatively high in September, defying President Trump's efforts to narrow it through tariffs.

stories.headline: Credit traders bet on data-center slowdown after Democratic sweep
stories.summary: Credit investors are positioning around how a Democratic Congress could slow data-center approvals, picking winners and losers among companies tied to AI infrastructure buildouts; FT similarly noted hyperscalers surging while chipmakers fell on bets about a Democratic backlash against the AI boom.

stories.headline: Kraft Heinz to divest North American coffee business in $650 million deal
stories.summary: Kraft Heinz agreed to sell its North American coffee business to private equity firm One Rock Capital Partners as CEO Steve Cahillane continues efforts to turn the company around.

Business.gaps: The Information and Forbes (beyond one CVS-related piece) had no additional distinct business-news items visible; Puck's visible content was mostly older than 48 hours, so no current Puck story could be confirmed for this period.

US politics.overview: Nearly every outlet in this group is leading with the same story: a historic Democratic sweep in Tuesday's midterms that flipped both chambers of Congress and several deep-red states, delivering a stinging rebuke to President Trump. Coverage is converging on the scale of the 'blue wave,' Texas's dramatic flip, looming Democratic investigations of the Trump administration, and the string of historic firsts among winning candidates.

stories.headline: Democrats sweep both chambers of Congress in historic midterm rout
stories.summary: Axios reports Democrats are projected to win at least 257 House seats to Republicans' 178 and at least 54 Senate seats, a landslide that exceeded even the most bullish pre-election forecasts and will usher in two years of investigations and legislative gridlock for Trump.

stories.headline: Texas turns blue for the first time in decades
stories.summary: Politico reports Democrats seized Texas after Republicans had run the country's second most-populous state for 30 years, with Gina Hinojosa winning the governorship and James Talarico defeating Ken Paxton for Senate, marking the first Texas Democrat elected to the chamber since 1988.

stories.headline: Democrats signal wave of investigations and subpoenas against Trump
stories.summary: RealClearPolitics notes Democrats in the House and Senate will gain subpoena power in January to investigate Trump and his administration on multiple fronts, a sentiment echoed by Sen. Ed Markey's "Subpoenas" post and incoming Oversight chair Robert Garcia's call to "lawyer up."

stories.headline: Trump accepts results, blames Iran war partly for GOP losses
stories.summary: WSJ reports Trump acknowledged the Iran war contributed to Republican losses as Democrats took Congress, while separately saying the U.S. plans to cut off military aid to Israel by year's end.

stories.headline: Hakeem Jeffries poised to become first Black House speaker
stories.summary: NPR reports that as speaker, Jeffries would be second in the presidential line of succession and has vowed to focus on affordability and holding the administration accountable.

stories.headline: Democrats set to win majority of U.S. governorships for first time in 16 years
stories.summary: Stateline reports Democrats are poised to control the majority of governors' offices after the GOP suffered major losses nationwide, including historic firsts such as the nation's first Black woman governor and first Native American woman governor.

stories.headline: Supreme Court rejects Trump DOJ bid to intervene in California ballot dispute
stories.summary: SCOTUSblog reports the Court declined to intervene in California's ballot dispute just before Election Day, denying a last-ditch Trump administration effort, with more voting-related battles potentially ahead.

stories.headline: Voters nationwide reject data center buildouts in local elections
stories.summary: Stateline reports that 33 local ballot measures to restrict data center construction passed Tuesday night, reflecting widespread voter backlash against the AI infrastructure boom.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS had no fresh midterm-results coverage available; its most recent relevant piece predates election night. Politico, NYT, WSJ, and The Guardian coverage is limited to the feed items provided since these outlets block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from this week's US midterm elections, which delivered a Democratic sweep seen as a major threat to the AI data-center buildout and hyperscaler capex, sending credit and equity markets into a scramble to reprice AI-exposed stocks. Anthropic's revised IPO filing—with its eye-popping compute commitments and an admission it may be nearing self-improving AI—is the other dominant thread, alongside backlash over Google's plan to tie school search access to AI adoption.

stories.headline: Democratic midterm sweep rattles the AI data-center boom
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that data center developers in Texas, already facing a suspension of approvals under outgoing Republican Governor Greg Abbott, are now bracing for an even tougher environment after Democrat Gina Hinojosa was elected as the state's first Democratic governor in decades. Credit traders are already betting on a data-center slowdown hurting developers, while hyperscaler shares jumped as investors bet a Democrat-controlled Congress will curb AI capex.

stories.headline: Anthropic's revised IPO filing reveals $895B in spending commitments and RSI warning
stories.summary: Anthropic's updated S-1 filing disclosed roughly $895 billion in compute and infrastructure commitments against Q3 revenue of nearly $17 billion, with the filing warning that its explosive revenue growth rate is unlikely to continue. In the same filing, Anthropic cautioned it may be nearing its own threshold for AI capable of recursive self-improvement, a watershed admission TechCrunch flagged from the document's risk-factors section.

stories.headline: Google's plan to cut school search access over AI restrictions sparks backlash
stories.summary: Google is bundling AI Overviews into core search for schools, prompting parents and educators to worry that machine-generated answers are undermining students' learning. Politicians including NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani and former FTC chair Lina Khan accused Google of acting as an unregulated monopoly after it emerged schools that fully block AI will lose access to search entirely starting in 2027.

stories.headline: Sequoia Capital unwinds 20 years of expansion
stories.summary: Sequoia is consolidating into a smaller, Bay Area-centered firm, shutting down the programs and offices it built during a 20-year expansion while announcing roughly $10 billion in new funds, including closing its Arc accelerator and Scouts program and merging its early-stage and growth teams.

stories.headline: NYT sues Brave over paywall blocker and AI content deals
stories.summary: The New York Times is suing browser maker Brave, with the lawsuit characterizing the company as a "supplier, dealer, and distributor" of stolen news content and demanding it shut down its paywall-bypass tool and end deals supplying content to AI firms.

stories.headline: Apple slashes engineers' daily AI spending caps amid cost-cutting fears
stories.summary: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple cut some engineers' daily AI spending cap to $200 from $300 and plans further cuts to as little as $100, fueling staff fears of layoffs as the cost-cutting push continues.

stories.headline: OpenAI acquires Pierre Computer Company to bolster coding agent infrastructure
stories.summary: OpenAI announced it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, the startup whose libraries already power its Codex coding agent, as the company builds out Git infrastructure to keep pace with AI coding agents following its recent Pando backend launch.

stories.headline: Anthropic unveils FlashProve, a cryptographic system to verify which AI model produced an output
stories.summary: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source research prototype offering "provable inference" — a cryptographic guarantee that a given AI output came from a specific model — intended to stop labs from secretly swapping in cheaper or more expensive models than advertised. The company stressed this is early-stage research with no current deployment plans.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer, Google DeepMind, Rest of World, and IEEE Spectrum had no substantive new AI/tech news in the search results or feed beyond routine/older items; The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist and The Guardian coverage is limited to what appeared in the provided feed since those outlets block direct search.

Energy.overview: Coverage across energy and climate outlets is dominated by the fallout from the US midterm elections, where a Democratic sweep of Congress was widely tied to voter anger over gas prices and the Iran war, triggering a sharp plunge in oil prices. Trade press like Utility Dive and Latitude Media are also tracking how the 'blue wave' will reshape state-level energy and utility policy, while Carbon Brief focuses on COP30 preparations in Brazil.

stories.headline: Oil tumbles as Democratic sweep of Congress piles pressure on Trump over Iran war
stories.summary: JD Vance publicly blamed the Iran war for the Republicans' midterm defeat as oil prices fell sharply on hopes that a Democratic-controlled Congress would push to end the conflict.

stories.headline: How Democrats' midterm sweep will rewire energy and data center policy
stories.summary: Latitude Media details how upset Democratic wins in Texas, Ohio, Wisconsin, Georgia and Nevada governor's races were driven by candidates campaigning on data-center moratoriums and utility accountability, with new governors like Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia pledging a year-long ban on data center construction.

stories.headline: Trump goes into the midterms with a gas price record
stories.summary: Heatmap reports that the average U.S. gasoline price hit $3.46 a gallon on the eve of the midterms, a record for Trump's second term, before oil prices plunged on hopeful signals from Iran peace talks.

stories.headline: Iran turns to guerrilla tactics to reassert grip on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: WSJ reports Tehran is using tactics including rocket-propelled grenades and limpet mines to disrupt the flow of oil through the Strait of Hormuz, a continuing threat to global crude supplies.

stories.headline: What's in the global 'roadmap' for transitioning away from fossil fuels?
stories.summary: Ahead of COP30, Brazil has produced a first-of-its-kind global roadmap on transitioning away from fossil fuels, which Carbon Brief describes as framing the shift as urgent but achievable.

stories.headline: Arizona utility APS plans to extend coal use to 2038 as demand set to double
stories.summary: Arizona Public Service expects peak demand to grow about 3.4% annually over the next 15 years, driven by industry and data centers, and has proposed extending coal plant operations as a result.

stories.headline: Trump's ban on foreign grid components sparks industry concern
stories.summary: Utility stakeholders have applauded the intent to secure the grid but warned that restrictions based on country of origin rather than function or capability could threaten investment.

stories.headline: Amid a blue wave, voters rebuke monopoly utilities in Georgia and Michigan
stories.summary: Georgia's Public Service Commission flipped to Democratic control for the first time in two decades, while Michigan voters approved a ballot measure banning utilities like DTE Energy from donating to state politicians, both reflecting backlash over rate hikes.

Energy.gaps: No stories meeting the last-24-48h window were found from E&E News, Canary Media, or Argus Media; available E&E News and Canary Media search results were weeks to months old. The Economist's energy-specific midterm coverage was limited to general political analysis rather than energy-focused pieces.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across Chinese, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Western financial outlets centers on Beijing's push to stabilize a battered stock market, the opening of the Shanghai import expo (CIIE) amid a flurry of foreign-leader visits, and ripple effects from the U.S. midterm elections on China trade policy. Business and tech outlets are also closely tracking a wave of Chinese AI model launches (Tencent, DeepSeek) and corporate anti-graft prosecutions.

stories.headline: China deploys liquidity tools and rate cuts to prop up stock market
stories.summary: China's central bank said it will conduct swap operations that could inject over $15 billion into the struggling stock market, after the benchmark CSI300 index posted its worst month since early 2016; Caixin separately reported the PBOC also cut its stock buyback relending rate to a record-low 1% as banks sought more than 200 billion yuan in quotas.

stories.headline: Ninth China International Import Expo opens in Shanghai amid wave of foreign leader visits
stories.summary: State-run Global Times reports the CIIE opens Thursday in Shanghai with 162 countries and over 4,100 overseas companies, coinciding with visits from leaders including Austria's chancellor, as Beijing frames the event as proof it remains committed to open markets despite rising global protectionism. Caixin's weekly preview separately flagged the same week as featuring state visits from Oman and Austria alongside the expo.

stories.headline: Democratic sweep in US midterms raises questions for China trade policy
stories.summary: SCMP reports that the Democrats' sweeping midterm victory could embolden Congress to assert greater authority over trade policy and scrutinize the trade deals President Trump struck with Beijing. Nikkei Asia also ran explainers on what the midterm results mean for Asia and for the broader US-China AI race.

stories.headline: Former China Eastern chairman sentenced to 14 years for bribery
stories.summary: A Chinese court sentenced Liu Shaoyong, former chairman of state-owned China Eastern Air Holding, to 14 years in prison for accepting more than 67.5 million yuan ($10.1 million) in bribes over two decades atop two major state airlines.

stories.headline: Hong Kong posts strongest GDP growth in five years
stories.summary: Hong Kong Free Press reports the city recorded GDP growth of over 5% in the first three quarters of 2026, the strongest pace of growth in five years.

stories.headline: DeepSeek reportedly to train next-gen V5 model on Huawei Ascend chips
stories.summary: TechNode reports DeepSeek plans to use Huawei's Ascend chips to train its next-generation V5 model, according to industry sources, a move that would deepen Chinese AI firms' reliance on domestic chips amid US export controls.

stories.headline: Fujian names former banker as acting governor in reshuffle
stories.summary: Guo Ningning, a former senior banker at Bank of China and Agricultural Bank, was named acting governor of Fujian province, putting her on track to be the first woman born in the 1970s to hold full provincial rank in China.

stories.headline: China seeks arrest of five Uyghurs detained for over a decade in Thailand
stories.summary: Hong Kong Free Press reports that five Uyghurs who have been detained in Thailand since 2014 are subject to Chinese arrest warrants, with Bangkok's security chief saying a Thai court will decide whether they are returned to China.

China.gaps: No recent coverage found via search for Sixth Tone, Rest of World, Xinhua, CGTN, Yicai Global or ChinaTalk; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, WSJ, Bloomberg and The Economist block search so only feed items (limited to two Economist pieces) were available for them.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf, Israeli and pan-Arab outlets is dominated by the fallout from the US midterms, with Trump and Vance openly blaming the Iran war for the Republican rout and oil markets swinging wildly on hopes the conflict may wind down. A parallel storyline is unfolding in Israel, where Netanyahu is contesting his election loss by alleging Qatari-backed foreign interference, even as US officials signal a pullback in military aid to Israel and sanctions pressure on Iran's sanctions-evasion networks continues.

stories.headline: Trump and Vance concede Iran war cost Republicans the midterms
stories.summary: JD Vance said Republicans lost control of Congress because of the Iran war, with Trump himself acknowledging the conflict was 'part of' the defeat even as he called it worth the cost; Vance argued voters wanted to 'change our relationship to Israel.'

stories.headline: Oil swings wildly as traders bet on an end to the Iran war after Democratic sweep
stories.summary: Crude prices whipsawed this week, sliding to a near four-week low before rebounding as Washington's next move on Iran remains unclear following the midterms, with Brent trading in the $94-$104 range.

stories.headline: Netanyahu alleges foreign interference as Shin Bet probes Qatari funding of Arab vote
stories.summary: Netanyahu said there are 'serious suspicions' foreign money swayed last week's election and insisted the Shin Bet probe into alleged Qatari funding of Arab parties must proceed, even as election officials and Qatar reject claims the vote was 'stolen.'

stories.headline: Trump says US plans to cut off military aid to Israel by year's end
stories.summary: President Trump said on election day that Washington and Israel have reached a 'deal' to end roughly $4 billion in annual US military aid within two months, a move that could come far faster than previously discussed.

stories.headline: US sanctions Indian and Turkish firms for aiding Iran's sanctions-evasion networks
stories.summary: The US Treasury issued fresh sanctions on companies and individuals in India and Turkey, targeting what it called a vast criminal network supporting Iran's oil trade.

stories.headline: Iran turns to guerrilla tactics in Hormuz, courts China and Russia for leverage
stories.summary: Tehran is deploying rocket-propelled grenades and limpet mines to disrupt oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, while separately seeking Chinese and Russian backing to guarantee any US sanctions-relief deal tied to its nuclear concessions.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco profits hold up despite being 'besieged by war'
stories.summary: The Economist reports that higher oil prices driven by the Iran conflict have comfortably offset the cost of bombed facilities, keeping Aramco's profits flowing.

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi's Ta'ziz raises $1.39bn for two Ruwais petrochemical projects
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi's Ta'ziz industrial platform secured $1.39 billion in financing for two projects at its Ruwais chemicals hub, underscoring continued Gulf investment even amid regional conflict.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not independently verify coverage from Gulf News, Khaleej Times, Arabian Business, AGBI, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, The New Arab, Ynetnews, and Haaretz beyond what surfaced in searches (mostly oil-price wire stories); Reuters, AP, NYT and BBC block search and had no relevant feed items provided beyond what's cited above.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage across these outlets this week centers on South Africa's pivotal municipal elections, the deepening Ethiopia-Eritrea standoff and its economic fallout, and the ripple effects of the US midterms on Washington's Africa policy and trade ties. Business and finance outlets are also tracking Nigeria's Dangote refinery IPO, a DRC mining crackdown, and US sanctions touching Rwanda, while health reporting flags progress on Ebola vaccines amid the ongoing DRC outbreak.

stories.headline: South Africans vote in local elections with ANC missteps in sharp focus
stories.summary: South Africans went to the polls Wednesday in municipal elections seen as a major test for the ANC, which has governed since the end of apartheid; analysts expect no outright majorities in many regions, forcing difficult coalition talks afterward.

stories.headline: Could conflict derail Ethiopia's economic reform agenda?
stories.summary: Renewed fighting between Ethiopia and Eritrea-aligned forces in Tigray threatens to unwind years of liberalization that helped Ethiopia attract billions in foreign investment, with one Oxford-linked study estimating a wider war could cost the economy over $100bn by 2027. Africa Confidential separately warns the two countries are edging toward a wider confrontation.

stories.headline: South Africa says US shifted goalposts on AGOA; Rwanda less affected
stories.summary: Pretoria says Washington changed the criteria used to justify excluding South Africa from the AGOA trade preference program, a decision it calls unfair, while noting Rwanda has been comparatively insulated from the fallout.

stories.headline: US midterms: 5 questions on what's at stake for Africa after Democrats' historic victory
stories.summary: The shift in US congressional power is expected to bring fresh scrutiny of the Trump administration's Africa policy, from foreign aid cuts to critical minerals deals; a companion piece notes Delaware Democrat Chris Coons, a longtime Africa advocate, now chairs the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.

stories.headline: Dangote refinery's $1.6 billion IPO draws nearly triple demand
stories.summary: Nigerian investors placed roughly $4.78 billion in orders for the Dangote refinery's planned November listing, far exceeding the offer size, underscoring strong local appetite for the oil giant's shares.

stories.headline: Washington's sanctions expose competing western policies on Kagame
stories.summary: New US restrictions on Rwanda's defence ministry and M23 financing come as five EU governments weigh a migration pact with Kigali, highlighting diverging Western approaches to President Paul Kagame amid the eastern Congo conflict.

stories.headline: Congo to probe illegal mining after seizing copper and cobalt
stories.summary: Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo seized thousands of tons of copper and cobalt, prompting the justice minister to order an investigation into allegations of widespread illegal mining.

stories.headline: WHO approves trials for two new Ebola vaccines
stories.summary: The World Health Organization has cleared trials of two vaccines designed for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola that has killed more than 5,300 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Africa.gaps: The Continent's site returned only older archived issues (back to August/May) with no distinct new stories in the last 48 hours; Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block search so only feed items (none provided for this group) could be checked, meaning their current Africa coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Coverage across media-industry outlets is dominated by the fallout from Tuesday's US midterms, with deep dives into how cable and broadcast news networks handled a Democratic sweep, how media stocks reacted, and how figures like Trump and conservative pundits are processing the result. Alongside the election aftermath, outlets are tracking structural industry stories: publishers' fraught relationship with Meta and AI platforms, The New York Times' subscriber growth, Fox News' ratings erosion, and a UK press-freedom legal fight.

stories.headline: Networks' contrasting midterm election-night coverage draws scrutiny
stories.summary: TheWrap contrasted Fox News' soul-searching tone with CNN's data-driven approach as the networks grappled on-air with a bigger-than-expected Democratic sweep, including a notable on-air exchange between Trump and Bret Baier. Mediaite separately flagged a hot-mic moment of Baier discussing on-air 'spin,' while NYT noted the mood swung from celebratory on MS NOW to regretful on Fox.

stories.headline: Media stocks surge in post-election rally
stories.summary: Deadline reported that media and broader markets rallied after the midterm results, with Elon Musk wryly joking about his unsuccessful spending to back conservative candidates.

stories.headline: Publishers accuse Meta of 'holding them over a barrel' on new terms
stories.summary: The News Media Association's chief executive is pressing the UK government to back its competition watchdog against Meta's new terms for publishers, calling the platform's leverage unfair.

stories.headline: AI news-licensing fights escalate: new lawsuits against Brave and Anthropic
stories.summary: Press Gazette's running tracker shows US newspapers including the New York Times and Chicago Tribune suing browser maker Brave for allegedly scraping content for AI firms, while Canadian publishers have filed suit against Anthropic and Microsoft struck its first Asia-Pacific news deal with Nine Entertainment.

stories.headline: New York Times on pace to hit 15 million subscribers by end of 2027
stories.summary: Nieman Lab reports the Times added 420,000 digital subscribers in the third quarter of 2026, keeping the company on track toward its long-stated subscription goal.

stories.headline: What's behind Fox News' steep ratings decline
stories.summary: TheWrap examined Fox News' loss of 27% of its total-day viewers in October even as the network's underlying financials, including ad and distribution revenue, remained strong; the piece also notes People Inc. cut 195 jobs this week as part of a broader publishing restructuring.

stories.headline: Judge rules against 'famous man' but ITN/Guardian injunction stays pending appeal
stories.summary: A UK court ruled against an unnamed public figure seeking to block an ITN/Guardian story about abuse of power, though the injunction remains in place while he appeals, with the man having argued publication could prompt him to take his own life.

stories.headline: CBS News becomes a proxy for the industry's broader anxieties
stories.summary: Puck's media columnist argues that the personnel drama at Bari Weiss's CBS News reflects wider anxieties gripping the news business, alongside notes on Kalshi's push to be seen as a journalistic sentiment barometer despite most of its bets being on sports.

Media.gaps: No usable recent items were found for NYT, WSJ, FT, or The Guardian beyond the single NYT feed item provided, since these outlets block web search; broader coverage from them could not be verified.
